**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of these topics.

**Topic 1.** Write an imaginary account of your first journey to Zambia; you may imagine how you travelled, the people you met, what surprised you and what probably amused you.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (récit imaginaire, article de journal, essai argumentatif classique, lettre de candidature) que le contenu. Un récit imaginaire se raconte à la première personne, avec une progression chronologique claire ; un article de journal scolaire présente un point de vue avec un titre et un ton engageant pour un lectorat de camarades ; un essai « discuss the advantages and disadvantages » exige d'examiner les deux faces du sujet avant de conclure ; une lettre de candidature respecte la structure administrative (adresses, objet, formule d'appel et de politesse) tout en mettant en valeur les qualités du candidat. Comme le sujet propose un choix entre quatre formats, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Imaginary narrative (modèle, environ 270 mots)

I still remember my first journey to Zambia as if it happened yesterday, even though it exists only in my imagination for now.

I travelled by road from Cameroon, crossing several countries before finally reaching the Zambian border, tired but thrilled at the sight of the "Welcome to Zambia" sign. The first thing that struck me was the sheer size of the Zambezi River, which I saw properly for the first time when we stopped near Victoria Falls. The roaring sound of the water was so loud that our guide had to shout to be heard, and the mist rising from the falls could be seen from kilometres away.

In Livingstone, I met a family who insisted on hosting me for the night, even though we had only just met at a local market. They cooked a delicious dish of nshima, a maize-based staple similar to our own "fufu," and I was amused to discover how many small habits, from greeting elders to sharing food from a common plate, felt instantly familiar despite being in a country I had never visited before.

What surprised me most was how many languages I heard spoken within a single day, Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga and English, often switched between mid-conversation without anyone seeming to notice. It reminded me that, like Cameroon, Zambia carries an enormous internal diversity that outsiders rarely imagine when thinking of "Africa" as a single place.

By the time I left, a week later, I no longer felt like a foreigner passing through, but like someone who had briefly become part of a community that had welcomed me without hesitation. That first journey to Zambia taught me more about hospitality than any book ever could.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of these topics.

**Topic 2.** "Nobody is above the law and nobody is below it in Cameroon." Do you agree with this assertion? Write an article in your school newspaper. You should call yourself Santiago Justice.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - School newspaper article (modèle, environ 260 mots)

**Is the Law Really the Same for Everyone in Cameroon?**

By Santiago Justice

The saying "Nobody is above the law and nobody is below it in Cameroon" sounds reassuring, but does it truly reflect our daily reality? I would argue that, in principle, it should be true, but in practice, it remains an ideal we are still working towards.

On paper, our legal system does apply the same rules to every citizen, regardless of wealth, status or family connections. Courts exist, laws are written, and in many ordinary cases, justice is indeed served fairly and efficiently, protecting citizens from abuse and settling disputes as it should.

However, we have all heard of cases where wealthy or well-connected individuals seem to escape consequences that would immediately affect an ordinary citizen in the same situation. A businessman with the right connections might see a case quietly dropped, while someone without such influence faces the full weight of the law for a similar offence. This gap between the law as written and the law as applied is precisely where the assertion breaks down.

I do not believe this means our legal system is fundamentally broken; rather, it means that turning the ideal into a lived reality requires constant vigilance from citizens, journalists and honest officials willing to expose favouritism wherever it appears.

I agree with the assertion as a goal we must keep striving towards, even while acknowledging that we are not there yet. Recognising the gap is the first step towards closing it.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of between 250 and 300 words on any one of these topics.

**Topic 3.** Write an essay in which you discuss the advantages and the disadvantages of travelling to other countries.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Discussion essay (modèle, environ 280 mots)

Travelling to other countries has become increasingly common, and like most experiences, it carries both real benefits and genuine drawbacks worth examining carefully.

Among the advantages, travelling broadens one's understanding of the world in a way no book can fully replace. Meeting people from different cultures, tasting unfamiliar food, and observing how other societies organise their daily lives challenges assumptions we did not even know we held. Travel can also open professional doors, since employers increasingly value candidates who have proven their adaptability by living or working in unfamiliar environments. Finally, for many people, travel is simply a source of joy and renewal, offering a break from routine that improves both mental and physical wellbeing.

However, travelling also has its disadvantages. It can be expensive, putting genuine international travel out of reach for many families, which raises questions about whose horizons actually get broadened by this experience. Travel can also expose people to real risks: unfamiliar diseases, political instability in some regions, or simple misunderstandings caused by not knowing local customs, which can occasionally lead to embarrassing or even dangerous situations. Finally, frequent travel, when not managed carefully, can create a sense of rootlessness, making it harder to build the kind of long-term relationships and community ties that come from staying in one place for an extended period.

On balance, I believe the advantages of travelling outweigh the disadvantages, provided one travels with adequate preparation, a genuine respect for local customs, and realistic expectations about both the risks and the discomforts involved. Like most valuable experiences, it rewards those who approach it thoughtfully rather than carelessly.

### Piège à éviter
Sur un sujet « discuss the advantages and disadvantages », se contenter d'énumérer un seul camp (par exemple uniquement les avantages) est sanctionné : il faut impérativement développer les deux faces avant de conclure par une position personnelle.

### Conseil
Structure toujours ce type d'essai en trois blocs clairement séparés : un paragraphe pour les avantages, un pour les inconvénients, puis un dernier paragraphe de synthèse qui prend position. Cette organisation, visible dès la lecture, rassure le correcteur sur la maîtrise du format attendu.

**Topic 4.** "The Voice of The People", a daily newspaper in Yaoundé, needs the services of a young bilingual (French and English) Cameroonian. You are interested in the job. Write an application to the manager. Your name is Nanga Marcel of Lycée de Bertoua, Box 35. You should try to convince the editor that you are young and dynamic and fit for the job.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 4 - Job application letter (modèle, environ 230 mots)

Nanga Marcel
Lycée de Bertoua
Box 35, Bertoua

The Manager
The Voice of The People
Yaoundé

Subject: Application for the position of bilingual journalist

Dear Sir,

I am writing to apply for the position of young bilingual Cameroonian recently advertised by your newspaper, The Voice of The People. I am a student at Lycée de Bertoua, fluent in both French and English, and firmly convinced that I have the energy and dedication this role requires.

Throughout my studies, I have consistently sought opportunities to strengthen both languages, contributing articles to my school magazine and taking part in bilingual debate competitions organised in my region. I believe this experience has prepared me well to write clearly and accurately for a bilingual readership such as yours.

Beyond my language skills, I am a naturally curious and hardworking young person, always eager to learn quickly and adapt to new environments and responsibilities. I am confident that my youthful energy, combined with the discipline instilled throughout my schooling, would allow me to make a genuine contribution to your team from the very first weeks.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application further at an interview, at your convenience. Please find below my contact details should you wish to reach me.

Thank you for considering my application.

Yours faithfully,

Nanga Marcel
